items.topic: Empty-state behavior when an initiative has no dependencies
items.context: Most initiatives won't declare depends_on. We need a consistent rule across CLI get, CLI list, UI detail, and UI list. Three reasonable patterns: omit the line/section entirely, show it with a placeholder like '(none)', or show it always but greyed out in UI / dim text in CLI.

options.label: Omit entirely when empty
options.rationale: Cleanest output, matches how most CLI tools handle empty optional fields, less visual noise. Recommended.

options.label: Always show, render '(none)' when empty
options.rationale: Discoverability — operators learn the field exists by seeing it. Costs a row of vertical space per initiative.

options.label: Show on `get` (always), omit on `list` when empty
options.rationale: Discoverability where space allows; compactness where it matters.

items.topic: Label wording (used identically across CLI and UI)
items.context: Pick once and apply everywhere. The spec proposes 'Depends on: a, b, c'. Alternatives have slightly different connotations.

options.label: 'Depends on'
options.rationale: Matches the field name and the spec's proposed wording. Reads naturally in a sentence and a column header. Recommended.

options.label: 'Dependencies'
options.rationale: Standard noun, very common in tooling. Slightly more formal; less obvious which direction (upstream vs downstream).

options.label: 'Upstream'
options.rationale: Disambiguates direction if we ever add a downstream view. Less self-explanatory to new operators.

items.topic: Also show downstream (what depends on this initiative)?
items.context: The spec only requests upstream (depends_on). Operators reasoning about portfolio readouts often want both directions. The API may or may not already return downstream — this is a scope-expansion question. Doing it now is cheap if the data is already there; otherwise it's a separate item.

options.label: Stick to upstream only (current spec)
options.rationale: Smallest, well-scoped fix matching the original problem statement. File a follow-up item if downstream display is wanted. Recommended.

options.label: Add downstream display in the same change, only if the API already returns it
options.rationale: Free win if the data is already present in the response payload. Adds CLI/UI surface and tests.

options.label: Add downstream display, computing it client-side from `initiatives list` if necessary
options.rationale: Most complete view. Larger scope, more code paths, more tests.

items.topic: Long dependency lists in CLI `initiatives list` rows
items.context: An initiative might depend on 5+ others. The list output is row-oriented and should stay scannable.

options.label: Comma-join all, no truncation
options.rationale: Simple, faithful, and the common case is 0-2 deps anyway. Recommended.

options.label: Truncate after 3 deps with '+N more'
options.rationale: Keeps row width predictable. Adds branching and a tiny formatter rule.

options.label: Wrap to a continuation line indented under the row
options.rationale: Most readable for many deps. Breaks one-row-per-initiative invariant some scripts may rely on.

items.text: spec.json already has acceptance_allow=['scenarios/swarm-manager/**']; not generating a decision for it. acceptance_deny is left empty — no protected paths inside this fix's surface.

Item has no `initiative` field set, so initiative-context loading was skipped. If this should be grouped with other CLI/UI display fixes under an initiative, set it via `swarm-manager backlog update --data '{"initiative":"..."}'`.

Plan was authored in a workspace that does not contain the swarm-manager source (only agent-manager is present here). The executing agent must run in a workspace that has scenarios/swarm-manager/. File-level discovery (CLI formatter functions, UI components, existing test pattern) is deferred to that agent — concrete search hints are in plan.md § Current Technical Context.
